title: Precision handoff scheduler: minimize dequant overhead across prefill and decode
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Implement a runtime scheduler that performs an adaptive precision handoff between quantized and mixed-precision kernel paths to reduce dequantization overhead during prefill and decoding. The scheduler should reason about remaining sequence length, KV cache reuse, batching behavior, and hardware characteristics to decide: (a) whether to keep KV cache entries in INT8/FP8 and run quantized kernels for upcoming decode steps; (b) when to perform a minimal upfront dequantization and switch to mixed-precision kernels for latency-sensitive short decodes; and (c) when to amortize dequant work across large prefill windows. Target models: Llama-family and Mistral-like architectures. Target hardware: A100/H100-class GPUs and future tensor-core accelerators.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler merged behind feature-flag and enabled for selected inference configs
End-to-end p50/p95/p99 token latency measured on internal perf harness shows >=8% p99 improvement for long-prefill workloads and <=5% regression on short-turns workloads
Per-token GPU time and host CPU dequant time telemetry emitted (new metrics) and visible in console dashboard
No functional regressions on structured-output tests and knob to force always-dequant path for A/B testing
Automated unit and integration tests exercising handoff boundary conditions included
implementation_notes: Add KernelAdvisor interface extension: score(candidate_kernel, context) -> estimated_time_us, memory_cost
Introduce HandoffPlanner that samples short-term decode distribution and chooses dequant horizon (0 = always quantized; N tokens to dequantize upfront)
Implement lightweight amortized dequant stage that runs as background CUDA stream when predicted batch size >= threshold
Expose feature flag runtime.flags.precision_handoff and per-model artifact config precision_handoff: enabled|conservative|disabled
Update kernel registry to support ephemeral mixed-precision kernels that accept quantized KV without full pre-dequantization (fast path)
Add fallbacks: if runtime memory pressure or cache misses exceed threshold, revert to conservative dequant path
test_plan: Microbench: kernel-level timing comparing quantized vs mixed-precision for single attention heads across sequence lengths [8,32,128,512]
End-to-end: synthetic prefill + decode sessions with varying turn lengths to measure p99 latency and per-token cost
Chaos test: simulate GPU memory pressure and abrupt model switches to verify safe fallback
Regression: run existing structured-output eval suite and embeddings/decoding correctness tests
A/B rollout: enable adaptive handoff for 5% of hosted traffic on dedicated rigs and compare business metrics
